newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore minister attacks absent opposition figure.
newsitem.headline: Singapore minister attacks absent opposition figure.

text.p: An opposition politician's remarks that ruling party leaders wanted to ruin him with lawsuits were serious charges that might be cause for fresh legal action, a Singapore cabinet minister was quoted as saying.
The Straits Times said on Monday Singapore Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong told reporters that comments by Tang Liang Hong were "a very serious allegation".
The paper earlier quoted Tang as saying the legal action taken against him was politically motivated and designed to "bury him politically and financially".
Asked if Tang's statement could be cause for more defamation action, Lee said: "It may be. Our lawyers are looking at it."
Tang, a defeated Workers' Party candidate in a hotly contested constituency in Singapore's general election on January 2, is currently out of the country.

Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong, Senior Minister Lee Kuan Yew and six other leaders of the ruling People's Action Party (PAP) filed defamation suits against Tang for calling them liars during the election campaign.

He faces other suits from PAP leaders as well, including action by Deputy Prime Minister Lee, Lee Kuan Yew's oldest son, over a report Tang lodged with police during the campaign which was re-published in various newspapers.
Lee Hsien Loong was quoted as repeating assurances that Tang would not be arrested under Singapore's Internal Security Act if he returned to Singapore.
Lee said Tang was "just producing more and more excuses to be some other place in the world".
Lee's office could not be immediately reached for comment on the Straits Times report.
